topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic and sets expectations regarding the complexity and importance of complement.

topics.label: Foundational principles and core mechanics of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the overall framework, naming conventions, and central role of component C3 in the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct upstream recognition pathways and the threshold mechanisms that trigger complement activation.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three primary downstream mechanisms executed by activated complement to destroy pathogens and stimulate immunity.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory factors and mechanisms that prevent complement activation from damaging healthy host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how genetic or acquired deficiencies in individual complement components lead to specific disease presentations.

topics.label: Pathogen strategies for complement evasion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the diverse molecular mechanisms evolved by pathogens like Staphylococcus aureus to circumvent complement defenses.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the complement lecture and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
